soundness_flags.label: def:efficient-score-handle; symbol \(\varphi_\omega^\star\); thm:efficient-eif-bound
soundness_flags.one_line: The handle defines \(\beta_{\omega,P}\), \(\varphi_\omega^\star\), its mean-zero property, and its pathwise derivative identity—the substantive assertions repeated by Theorem 1—so the claimed canonical-gradient theorem is currently a definitional restatement rather than a derived DDD result.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:crossfit-attainment / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The inference claim is conditional on fixed \(T\), fixed aggregate support and joint residual dimension, nonsingular conditional covariance, and the displayed rate-indexed attainment class \(\mathcal M_n\).
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform attainment and Wald coverage are claimed only over these fixed-dimensional triangular subclasses, excluding unbalanced panels, repeated cross-sections, adaptive weights, singular covariance, and violations of conditional DDD parallel trends.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published abstract states that the article computes semiparametric efficiency bounds for finite-dimensional parameters under sequential moment restrictions with unknown functions and presents an optimally weighted orthogonalized estimator.
The article develops Neyman-orthogonal scores and cross-fitting for high-dimensional nuisance estimation, but does not provide a DDD shared-covariance efficiency result.

The paper defines stacked DDD with eligible and ineligible cells, states that ineligible units are unaffected by the policy, and characterizes stacked DDD as trading efficiency for regression transparency and pairwise interpretation when controls are shared.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the definitionally certified EIF with an unnamed candidate score; remove the imposed mean-zero and pathwise-derivative equalities, then prove those identities from an explicit observable DDD conditional-moment representation and establish existence of the projection coefficient.

After deriving the score, state a DDD-specific closed-form or finite-dimensional algorithm for its projection and use it in the cross-fitted estimator, rather than defining the estimator through a score whose required properties are already assumed.

Make the field contribution non-routine by proving a generic shared-comparison precision comparison against both Ortiz-Villavicencio–Sant'Anna constant GMM and Hsieh stacked DDD, with the conditional-GLS loss formula as a corollary.

recommended_next_step: Revise the efficient-score construction so Theorem 1 derives, rather than defines, the canonical gradient; then rerun the field-tier novelty review.
